title: What is mental health?
citation: Galderisi, S., Heinz, A., Kastrup, M., Beezhold, J., & Sartorius, N. (2015). Toward a new definition of mental health. World psychiatry, 14(2), 231.
content:
What is mental health?

Mental health can be seen as our psychological and emotional wellbeing. It influences how we cope with stress, build relationships, make decisions and manage everyday life. Mental health is something everyone has, just like physical health. It exists on a spectrum and naturally changes over time in response to life experiences, health, relationships and the environment.

Doesn't "mental health" just mean not having a mental illness?

A common misunderstanding is that mental health simply means the absence of a mental illness. Mental health is much broader than that. A person can be living with a mental health condition while still experiencing purpose, strong relationships and wellbeing. Likewise, someone without a mental illness may still struggle with stress, burnout, loneliness, or emotional exhaustion. Mental health is about overall wellbeing, not simply whether a condition is present.

Why does my mental health change from day to day?

Mental health is shaped by many interacting factors, including sleep, physical health, stress, social connection, work, hormones and major life events. Because these factors are constantly changing, it is normal for mental health to fluctuate as well. Some days you may feel resilient and motivated, while on others you may feel emotionally drained or less able to cope. These changes are part of being human and do not necessarily mean something is wrong.

What does good mental health actually feel like?

Good mental health does not mean feeling happy all the time or never experiencing difficult emotions. Instead, it often means being able to experience a range of emotions, recover from setbacks, adapt to challenges and continue functioning in daily life. People with good mental health can still feel stressed, sad, or frustrated, but these feelings are usually manageable and do not completely take over their lives.

Mental health vs mental illness: what's the difference.

Mental health and mental illness are related, but they are not the same thing. Mental health refers to one's overall emotional, psychological and social wellbeing. Mental illness refers to specific health conditions that affect thoughts, emotions, or behaviour in ways that significantly interfere with daily life. Thinking of mental health as a spectrum helps explain why everyone can take steps to improve their wellbeing.

Why does my mental health dip even when life seems fine?

Many people are surprised when they notice their mental health decline despite nothing obviously going wrong. Mental wellbeing is influenced by factors that are not always visible, including ongoing stress, lack of quality sleep, physical health, hormonal changes, loneliness and accumulated life pressures. Sometimes several small challenges build up over time, making it difficult to identify one clear reason. The absence of an obvious cause does not make the experience any less real.

When should I pay attention to my mental health?

Looking after your mental health is important whether you are struggling or feeling well. It is worth paying closer attention if you notice persistent changes in your mood, stress levels, energy, sleep, relationships, or ability to cope with everyday responsibilities. Just as people look after their physical health before problems become serious, taking care of mental health early through healthy habits or professional support can improve wellbeing and help prevent difficulties from becoming more overwhelming.
